paper: Identification, evidence caps, and the price of shared randomness
subtitle: Orthogonal two-view fibers, persistent-latent evidence, and exact fair-bit costs in finite games
author: Jaden Fix

claims.name: fiber classification
claims.status: part (1) already in the repository; the orthogonal ambiguity is the standard symmetric-NMF fact; new: the stochastic reparametrization
assumptions: finite alphabets, k latent states with k fixed and known
prior pi strictly positive; row-stochastic channel K of full row rank k
exact population law of the two views across independent world draws
the same channel K for both views
nonclaims: alternatives with more than k latent states are not classified
an observer of a single world draw never sees the two-view law T

claims.name: strictly positive channels are not even locally identified
assumptions: finite alphabets, k latent states with k fixed and known
prior pi strictly positive; row-stochastic channel K of full row rank k
exact population law of the two views across independent world draws
K > 0 entrywise and k >= 2
nonclaims: no finite-sample estimator or confidence set is given

claims.name: what the earlier rigidity theorem excludes
claims.status: corollary; re-reads ST-T261 and P1-T7 of the companion paper
assumptions: finite alphabets, k latent states with k fixed and known
prior pi strictly positive; row-stochastic channel K of full row rank k
exact population law of the two views across independent world draws
nonclaims: does not change the scope of ST-T261, which remains correct as stated

claims.name: different channels per view
claims.status: part (a) and its dimension count are known (Henry-Kitamura-Salanie; Hall-Zhou); only (b) product-gauge rigidity is claimed
assumptions: two views with row-stochastic channels K_1, K_2 of full row rank k
strictly positive prior
nonclaims: part (a) is not new

claims.name: sharp identified set, k = 2
claims.status: known bounds specialized: specializes the sharp two-component bounds of Henry, Kitamura and Salanie (Thm. 1) to a shared channel; feasible-band construction of Lawton and Sylvestre; only the explicit closed form is offered, no priority claimed
assumptions: finite alphabets, k latent states with k fixed and known
prior pi strictly positive; row-stochastic channel K of full row rank k
exact population law of the two views across independent world draws
label convention: latent 1 favored by the extreme outcome x*
nonclaims: no finite-sample confidence interval for [L, U]

claims.name: an exact witness with a strictly positive alternative channel
assumptions: the declared pi = (9/25, 16/25) and 2 x 3 channel K
nonclaims: one instance; not a general bound

claims.name: weight floor
assumptions: finite alphabets, k latent states with k fixed and known
prior pi strictly positive; row-stochastic channel K of full row rank k
exact population law of the two views across independent world draws
nonclaims: the upper bound 1 - (k - 1) l(T) is not claimed sharp

claims.name: three latent states
assumptions: the declared pi = (1/9, 4/9, 4/9) and 3 x 4 channel
nonclaims: the k = 3 sharp set is not computed (open problem ST-O07); float estimates are uncertified

claims.name: two views plus anchors identify
claims.status: known mechanism: separability (anchor-word) mechanism of Donoho-Stodden and Arora-Ge-Kannan-Moitra; no priority claimed
assumptions: finite alphabets, k latent states with k fixed and known
prior pi strictly positive; row-stochastic channel K of full row rank k
exact population law of the two views across independent world draws
each latent has an anchor outcome in the true channel
nonclaims: anchor sufficiency is known
for k >= 3 anchors are not necessary (ST-M89)

claims.name: point identification without anchors
assumptions: pi uniform on three states and the declared 3 x 6 channel
nonclaims: does not characterize point identification for k >= 3

claims.name: a necessary condition for point identification
assumptions: finite alphabets, k latent states with k fixed and known
prior pi strictly positive; row-stochastic channel K of full row rank k
exact population law of the two views across independent world draws
nonclaims: necessary, not sufficient, for k >= 3

claims.name: three views identify (Kruskal)
claims.status: cited (Kruskal 1977; see Allman et al.; Anandkumar et al.); not reproved
assumptions: three conditionally independent views through the same channel
factor matrices of Kruskal rank k, k >= 2
nonclaims: cited, not proved in the repository or the paper

claims.name: the third view separates the witness pair
assumptions: the k = 2 witness pair of ST-M87
nonclaims: one instance; Kruskal's theorem is cited for the general statement

claims.name: Bayes factor one inside the fiber
claims.status: standard 'no learning about non-identified directions' fact (Dawid; Poirier); only its location inside the two-view fiber is new
assumptions: n IID two-view pairs
nonclaims: not new
the Giacomini-Kitagawa posterior limit is cited, not proved

claims.name: exact fiber audit
assumptions: rational arithmetic on declared grids and instances
nonclaims: finite checks corroborate proofs on bounded instances; they are not proofs

claims.name: persistent cap
claims.status: data-processing inequality; not new; contribution is the application to world-level weights
assumptions: shared kernel K
experimenter policy does not depend on the hypothesis label
N-unit form: independent world draws
nonclaims: bounds an expectation, not every transcript (that is ST-T226)
vacuous when a is not absolutely continuous with respect to b
does not limit learning which world is active

claims.name: saturation identity
claims.status: identity is the KL chain rule and the zero-gap condition specializes the Kullback-Leibler equality condition; only the finite-M ratio form is new
assumptions: KL(a || b) finite
finite M with component densities for the zero-gap condition
nonclaims: the converse of 'M a function of Y implies zero gap' fails in general

claims.name: gap bound and decay
claims.status: MAP-error exponent classical; only the (r_max / r_min - 1) factor and the support-mismatch term are new
assumptions: finite M with a absolutely continuous with respect to b
conditionally IID transcripts for the decay statement
relevant component pairs have distinct laws
nonclaims: the gap decays at least as fast as the stated exponent; the exponent is not shown tight

claims.name: different kernels
claims.status: chain rule plus data processing; standard
assumptions: the hypotheses may use different kernels
nonclaims: no matching lower bound

claims.name: exact persistent-latent audit
assumptions: exact laws over sufficient count vectors with 60-digit logarithms, declared examples up to n = 64
nonclaims: bounded corroboration, not a proof

claims.name: realizable laws
claims.status: elementary; no repository claim of its own
assumptions: b fair bits, or t uniform L-ary tosses, with L >= 2
nonclaims: not new

claims.name: dyadic dichotomy
assumptions: finite rational game; public seed seen before the source (A1)
adversary oblivious to the seed (A2)
rational payoffs with common denominator (A4)
fixed budget of b fair bits (A3)
nonclaims: extracting fair bits from a biased or physical source is not addressed

claims.name: two-sided gap without nondegeneracy assumptions
assumptions: finite rational game; public seed seen before the source (A1)
adversary oblivious to the seed (A2)
rational payoffs with common denominator (A4)
fixed budget of b fair bits (A3)
nonclaims: the upper constant is not claimed tight

claims.name: optimal exact sampling (Knuth-Yao)
claims.status: classical (Knuth and Yao 1976; entropy bounds from Cover and Thomas); reproved in the repository derivation behind the bit-price claims; not new
assumptions: exact sampling of a rational law from fair bits
nonclaims: classical; not claimed as new

claims.name: the price of the value
claims.status: new: composition of the Knuth-Yao cost with the optimal set
assumptions: finite rational game; public seed seen before the source (A1)
adversary oblivious to the seed (A2)
rational payoffs with common denominator (A4)
variable budget: IID fair bit stream and an almost surely finite stopping time (A3)
nonclaims: the minimum over a non-singleton optimal set is attained but not computed in general
private encoder randomness is not covered

claims.name: coins with L sides
assumptions: finite rational game; public seed seen before the source (A1)
adversary oblivious to the seed (A2)
rational payoffs with common denominator (A4)
integer L >= 2; t independent uniform L-sided tosses
nonclaims: no fairness of any real coin is certified

claims.name: the K3 value curve
assumptions: the K3 game: three point-mass scenarios and the three complete prefix codes with lengths a permutation of (1, 2, 2)
nonclaims: one game

claims.name: the skew total-variation game at radius one half
assumptions: the ST-M27 game: K3 graph, nominal prior (4/5, 1/10, 1/10), total-variation radius 1/2
nonclaims: one game

claims.name: Knuth-Yao prices of the committed instances
claims.status: exact instances; the 8/3-bit cost of a uniform ternary choice is classical
assumptions: the reduced games of the committed instances
nonclaims: the 8/3-bit cost is not new; only its identification as the exact coordination price of these games is offered

claims.name: one L-sided toss
assumptions: L <= 12 (and L^t <= 1000 for the K3 game when 3 does not divide L)
nonclaims: the general criterion is ST-T313; the instance checks are bounded

claims.name: exact certification of the bit price
assumptions: declared enumeration bounds (b <= 12 for K3, b <= 10 for committed matrices, seeded random games and laws, L <= 12)
nonclaims: bounded corroboration, not a proof; the congruence decision procedure is exact but bounded in the checker

claims.name: point identification and sharp sets for k >= 3
assumptions: finite alphabets, k latent states with k fixed and known
prior pi strictly positive; row-stochastic channel K of full row rank k
exact population law of the two views across independent world draws
nonclaims: a target, not a conclusion

claims.name: second-order term of the evidence constant
claims.status: open; formal expansion and numerics only
assumptions: interior beta
nonclaims: the remainder bounds are not written; numerical agreement is not a proof

context_note: cited in prose or in Appendix A as context; stated in the repository, not restated as a result block here
paper_nonclaims: nothing in the paper is evidence for or against simulation
reading a latent state as simulated versus base is an interpretation of the mixture model, not a finding
novelty is claimed only for the stated forms, with no claim of priority
